criteria.requirement: A useful four-track, sixteen-step sample with locally generated percussion, bass and melody can start after a user gesture without account/microphone/remote service.
criteria.action: Open the sample and start playback through a user gesture without account or microphone access.
criteria.expected: A four-track sixteen-step pattern with percussion, bass and melody is immediately playable without remote audio services; inaudible sound must remain unverified.

criteria.requirement: Grid editing is accessible by mouse/touch/keyboard with track names, playhead and clear on/off/focus states.
criteria.action: Edit grid steps with mouse, touch and keyboard and inspect focus and playhead.
criteria.expected: Track names, playhead and on/off/focus states are clear and all three input methods can edit steps.

criteria.requirement: Tempo, per-track volume, mute and solo have coherent playback and 3D note feedback.
criteria.action: Change tempo and each track's volume, mute and solo during playback.
criteria.expected: Playback state and instrument note feedback follow the controls; audio conclusions require actual listening evidence.

criteria.requirement: Pause retains position while stop returns to the first step; clear and restore-demo confirm replacing edited work.
criteria.action: Pause/resume, stop, edit a pattern, then cancel and confirm clear/restore-demo.
criteria.expected: Pause retains position, stop returns to the first step, and destructive replacement of edited work requires confirmation.

criteria.requirement: Rhythm uses an audio-clock schedule and 3D notes align with sounding notes without duplicate loops during tempo changes; do not infer audible fidelity from visuals alone.
criteria.action: Change tempo repeatedly during playback and compare actual audio with instrument motion if audible capture is available.
criteria.expected: Rhythm remains single and steady with note-aligned animation; audio-clock implementation and audible alignment stay unverified without suitable evidence.

criteria.requirement: Suspended/background audio has a truthful recoverable paused state, and stopping/leaving/switching patterns does not leave stuck notes.
criteria.action: Stop, switch patterns, leave/revisit the page and exercise suspended/background playback where observable.
criteria.expected: No stuck notes are observed; suspension is represented truthfully and explicit resume can recover playback. Unsupported audio/background probes remain unverified.

criteria.requirement: At least three named patterns can be saved, renamed, deleted and restored after refresh, with visible saved/dirty state.
criteria.action: Save at least three named patterns, rename and delete them, make an unsaved edit and refresh.
criteria.expected: Named patterns can be managed locally, saved/dirty state is shown and the last saved pattern restores after refresh.

criteria.requirement: Versioned JSON import/export validates tempo, tracks and step counts, rejects malformed input and preserves current work.
criteria.action: Export a pattern and import it, then try invalid tempo, track values and step counts.
criteria.expected: Versioned JSON restores valid patterns; malformed input gives useful errors and preserves the current work.

criteria.requirement: Compact layout keeps track names/transport reachable, supports reduced motion and textual playback status.
criteria.action: Use a phone viewport, enable reduced motion and inspect textual status during playback.
criteria.expected: Track names and transport stay reachable, status is readable and reduced motion retains note/playhead feedback without large instrument movements.

scenarios.instruction: Inspect the sample grid and instruments; start audio through the UI and observe note/playhead feedback.
Edit steps, tempo, mute/solo/volume and compare pause/resume with stop; save and rename a pattern.
Reload saved work, reject malformed import, exercise replacement confirmation and background/suspend recovery where observable; explicitly report any inability to hear audio.

Inspect a 390px-wide viewport, including lower controls and focus navigation. Perform the task through the primary UI without relying on precise 3D camera manipulation. Record any clipped, obstructed or unreachable content.
